Classify heart failure outcomes in claims data

Source: R/hf_outcomes.R
classify_hf_outcomes.Rd

Applies a version's heart failure outcome rules to diagnosis-level claims and returns one row per event. The rules come from the version's outcome code table (get_hf_v2_codes(variable_type = "outcome")), including its required_secondary and qualifies_as_primary columns, so what analysts see in the table is what is applied.

Two outcomes are classified, both only from claims strictly after the patient's reference date plus min_event_days:

  • acute_hf_hospitalization: an inpatient claim (claim_setting equal to any value of inpatient_setting) where either (a) the primary diagnosis is an acute or acute-on-chronic I50 code, or (b) the primary diagnosis is I11.0 and any I50 code is in a non-primary position, or the primary diagnosis is I13.0 or I13.2 and both an I50 and an N18 code are in non-primary positions.

  • incident_hf: the first claim (any setting, any diagnosis position) with any I50 code. It is incident only if the cohort excludes patients with heart failure before the reference date; see exclude_prevalent_hf.

The function does not remove prevalent heart failure, define the reference date, or define follow-up windows. Those belong to cohort construction.

Usage

classify_hf_outcomes(
  data,
  col_ref_date,
  outcomes = c("acute_hf_hospitalization", "incident_hf"),
  version = "v2",
  min_event_days = 0L,
  exclude_prevalent_hf = TRUE,
  col_patient_id = "patient_id",
  col_claim_id = "claim_id",
  col_dx_code = "dx_code",
  col_dx_position = "dx_position",
  col_claim_setting = "claim_setting",
  col_claim_date = "claim_date",
  inpatient_setting = "inpatient"
)

Arguments

data

A data frame or lazy table with one row per diagnosis per claim.

col_ref_date

Name of the column holding each patient's reference date, the date follow-up for events starts. Required. It should hold one date per patient, repeated on that patient's rows, with no missing values.

outcomes

One or both of "acute_hf_hospitalization" and "incident_hf".

version

Heart failure definition version, e.g. "v2" or 2. Only versions that define outcome rules are supported.

min_event_days

Whole number of days, at least 0 (default 0L). Only claims strictly after col_ref_date + min_event_days are classified.

exclude_prevalent_hf

If TRUE (default) and "incident_hf" is requested, the function errors when the input has any heart failure claim (any code in the outcome code table, any position and setting) strictly before col_ref_date. This only checks claims present in data, so pass the pre-reference claims along; filtering them out first makes the check pass without proving anything. Set to FALSE to skip the check, e.g. for studies of recurrent heart failure events. The check is not run when only "acute_hf_hospitalization" is requested.

col_patient_id, col_claim_id

Names of the patient and claim identifier columns. A claim is identified by the patient and claim IDs together.

col_dx_code

Name of the column with ICD-10-CM diagnosis codes in short format (no periods).

col_dx_position

Name of the integer column with the diagnosis position on the claim (1 is primary).

col_claim_setting

Name of the column with the claim setting. Acute hospitalizations are taken from claims whose setting is one of the values in inpatient_setting.

col_claim_date

Name of the date column with the claim's start date (the admission date for inpatient claims, the visit date for others).

inpatient_setting

One or more values of the claim setting column that identify overnight inpatient claims, e.g. c("inpatient_a", "inpatient_b") when inpatient stays are coded under several settings. Default "inpatient".

Value

A data frame (or lazy table, for lazy input) with one row per event and columns patient_id, outcome, claim_id, claim_date and qualifying_code, always under these names regardless of the col_* arguments. A claim can appear once per outcome. For acute_hf_hospitalization, qualifying_code is the primary diagnosis code. For incident_hf there is at most one row per patient, the first claim by date (then claim ID), and qualifying_code is the first I50 code on it alphabetically.

Details

data can be a local data frame or a lazy table (e.g., duckdb or Spark through dbplyr). Only dplyr verbs are applied, so lazy input stays lazy and a lazy table is returned. The validation checks run small queries that return counts (and, if the prevalent-HF check fails, a few example rows). With min_event_days > 0, date arithmetic is translated by the backend, so check it on backends other than duckdb.

Diagnosis codes must be ICD-10-CM in short format, with no periods ("I5021", not "I50.21"); other codes simply do not match. Version v2 is ICD-10 only, so claims before October 1, 2015 cannot be classified.

See also

get_hf_v2_codes()

Examples

claims <- data.frame(
  patient_id    = c(1, 1, 2, 2, 2),
  claim_id      = c("a", "b", "c", "c", "c"),
  claim_setting = c("outpatient", "inpatient", "inpatient", "inpatient", "inpatient"),
  claim_date    = as.Date(c("2024-01-10", "2024-03-01", rep("2024-02-05", 3))),
  ref_date      = as.Date("2024-01-01"),
  dx_position   = c(1, 1, 1, 2, 3),
  dx_code       = c("I509", "I5021", "I130", "I5022", "N184")
)
classify_hf_outcomes(claims, col_ref_date = "ref_date")
#> # A tibble: 4 × 5
#>   patient_id outcome                  claim_id claim_date qualifying_code
#>        <dbl> <chr>                    <chr>    <date>     <chr>          
#> 1          1 incident_hf              a        2024-01-10 I509           
#> 2          1 acute_hf_hospitalization b        2024-03-01 I5021          
#> 3          2 acute_hf_hospitalization c        2024-02-05 I130           
#> 4          2 incident_hf              c        2024-02-05 I5022
